verses.1: A wicked person who walks with integrity is better than a fool who speaks with his lips.
verses.2: A person without knowledge desires nothing, and one who stumbles with his feet commits sin.
verses.3: The folly of a person leads him astray in his path, and his heart resents the LORD.
verses.4: Wealth brings many friends, but the poor are separated even from their neighbor.
verses.5: A false witness will not go unpunished, and the one who lies in testimony will not escape.
verses.6: Many seek the favor of a noble, and all people are to a generous giver.
verses.7: All the brothers of the wicked hate him, and his neighbor is far from him; he calls them with words, but they are not there.
verses.8: A man who buys wisdom loves his own soul; one who guards understanding will find good.
verses.9: A false witness will not go unpunished, and the one who lies in testimony is ruined.
verses.10: It is not fitting for a fool to take pleasure, nor for a slave to rule over people.
verses.11: A person's wisdom makes his anger slow, and his glory is to overlook an offense.
verses.12: A king's rebuke is like the growl of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
verses.13: A foolish son is a disgrace to his father; a quarrelsome wife is like constant dripping.
verses.14: A house and wealth are inherited from ancestors, but a wise wife is from the LORD.
verses.15: Lazy hands cause poverty, and idle fingers bring hunger.
verses.16: One who keeps the commandment preserves his life, but the one who ignores his ways will die.
verses.17: One who lends to the LORD will be repaid, and he will repay the person fully.
verses.18: Discipline your son, for there is hope; do not set your heart on causing him to die.
verses.19: A hot-tempered man must bear the punishment; if you spare him, you will have to do so again.
verses.20: Listen to advice and accept instruction, so that you will be wise in the end.
verses.21: Many are the plans in a person's heart, but the counsel of the LORD is what stands.
verses.22: The desire of a person is his steadfast love, and the good of the upright is better than a deceitful person.
verses.23: The fear of the LORD is for life, and one who rests in it will not be found guilty of wrongdoing.
verses.24: A lazy man buries his hand in the dish, and even his mouth refuses to bring it back.
verses.25: A scoffer will be struck down, and a fool will be humbled; the one who corrects a wise person will gain understanding.
verses.26: One who robs his father and drives out his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
verses.27: My son, do not stop listening to instruction, so that you may avoid the words of knowledge.
verses.28: A witness who lies gives a false judgment, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.
verses.29: Punishments are prepared for scoffers, and beatings are for the foolish.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "wisdom makes his anger slow" reflects the metaphorical use of "sekel" as a measure of mental discernment.
- v. 23: "rests in it" is a natural rendering of "yalin" in the context of living securely.
- v. 25: "gain understanding" (from "yavin da'at") is a natural rendering of the Hebrew's emphasis on a wise person's comprehension.
- v. 28: "mouth of the wicked devours iniquity" captures the figurative sense of "yb'la awen," where "devour" reflects the Hebrew verb's intensity.
